record.paper_title: Geometric and Topological Obstructions to Various Immersions in Submanifold Theory and Some Related Open Problems
record.original_question: Is every compact finite-type hypersurface in Euclidean space necessarily a hypersphere?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 7.2. The only compact hypersurfaces of finite type in a Euclidean space are hyperspheres.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $x : M \to \mathbb{R}^m$ be an isometric immersion of a compact connected Riemannian manifold $M$ into Euclidean space. Decompose the position vector $x$ in terms of the spectral resolution of the Laplace–Beltrami operator $\Delta$ of $M$:
$$ x = x_0 + \sum_{i \in I} x_i, \qquad \Delta x_i = \lambda_i x_i, $$
where $x_0$ is a constant vector, the $\lambda_i$ are distinct nonzero eigenvalues of $\Delta$, and each $x_i$ is a nonconstant $\mathbb{R}^m$-valued eigenfunction. The immersion $x$ is said to be of finite type if the index set $I$ is finite; equivalently, there exists a polynomial $P$ such that $P(\Delta)(x - x_0) = 0$.

Now suppose $M^n$ is a compact hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ (i.e., $m = n+1$) and that the inclusion is of finite type in the sense above. Prove or disprove: $M$ must be a round hypersphere of $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is the well-known conjecture of B.-Y. Chen that the only compact finite-type hypersurfaces in a Euclidean space are hyperspheres. Surveys and recent works (e.g., on finite-type submanifolds and Chen's conjectures) note that the conjecture has been verified in several special cases (planar curves, certain low-dimensional or low-codimensional cases, hypersurfaces with restricted principal curvatures) but the general statement remains open.

status_evidence.title: Recent Developments in Chen's Biharmonic Conjecture and Some Related Topics
status_evidence.snippet: Chen posed problems on classifying finite type hypersurfaces in Euclidean space; circles are the only finite type closed planar curves, and very few examples of finite type hypersurfaces are known.
status_evidence.claim: The classification of compact finite-type hypersurfaces in Euclidean space remains a major open problem, with only limited examples known.

status_evidence.title: Tamkang J. Math. survey on finite type submanifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing Chen's conjecture that the only compact finite type hypersurfaces in Euclidean space are hyperspheres, with partial results.
status_evidence.claim: Chen's conjecture on compact finite-type hypersurfaces is documented as still open in survey literature.
